messages:
alex k.: Quick sync — we need to decide on a retention strategy for traces. Cost is creeping up and billing accuracy for tenant attribution is non-negotiable. Do we go TTL-heavy (keep everything short, then drop) or sampling + reconstruction for long tail? Thoughts?

ravi singh: My gut says hybrid. Keep full traces for error/SLO cohorts + business-critical tenants. For everything else: do sample + store light rollups (span counts, top-level durations, billing_key aggregates).

priya m.: Hybrid sounds okay but key risk is losing the billing_key during sampling. Our current span model attaches billing info on a later enrichment stage — if that gets sampled out, we lose attribution. We should canonicalize billing_key earlier (envelope/root) or replicate into earliest spans.

alex k.: Agree — moving billing_key into the envelope header would make sampling-safe attribution. That said we need to think about cardinality explosion if billing_key is high-cardinality (per-user). Priya — do you have a proposal for where exactly to put it?

priya m.: Proposal (small): put billing_key on the envelope and require the tracer SDK to copy it into the root span as `trace.attributes.billing_key`. Pipeline enrichment can then trust either envelope or root span. Example:```json
{
  "envelope": { "billing_key": "acct:acme-prod" },
  "spans": [ { "id": "...", "attributes": { "service": "api" } } ]
}
```This keeps downstream joins simple.

sarah j.: Two operational concerns: 1) we need a migration plan for older SDKs that don't set the envelope billing_key. 2) we should avoid making billing_key required in all indexes — it should be optional in active storage schema to avoid index bloat. Feature-flag rollout + schema versioning.

ravi singh: From pipeline side — this affects the ingest topic and enrichment stage. I suggest: new topic `trace-envelopes-v2` that carries billing_key at envelope level. Enrichment service subscribes to both v1 and v2; v1 triggers lookup/patch (cheap cache of billing_key->tenant) and v2 bypasses lookup. That keeps migration smooth.

alex k.: Good plan. Also think about sampling boundaries: if we allow partial traces (sampled spans), we must mark sampled traces with `sample.reason` and `sample.strategy` so downstream rollups know how to scale counts. Otherwise billing math will be wrong.

priya m.: +1. Add `sample.rate` (float) and `sample.reason` (enum: error/slo/initial/probabilistic) to envelope. That way rollups can inverse-scale metrics. But note: invert-scaling only safe if sampling is uniform. For non-uniform (error-focused), we must not rescale. So `sample.reason` must be respected.

eng-bot: RFC link posted: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/trace-ttl-and-sampling-2026 (document created by @alex k.).

alex k.: Action items: 1) priya — draft small RFC for envelope billing_key + sample metadata (target EOD Tue). 2) ravi — plan `trace-envelopes-v2` topic + enrichment fallback (target Wed). 3) sarah — schema migration playbook + index cost estimate (target Thu). We'll do a quick sync Friday. If anyone sees major holes call them out here. :thumbsup:

sarah j.: small note — add a check in the EL to deny billing_key values > 256 chars and normalize casing. Avoiding weird high-card keys will save indexes.

ravi singh: added. Also will include a cost projection table in the plan (hot vs cold storage) so PM can budget.

priya m.: sounds good. I'll start the RFC and include example patches for SDKs.

alex k.: Thanks all. Keeping this thread as the state for now.
